correctness.rationale: For alpha>-1, eta>0, 0<|epsilon|<1, beta-normalized radial monomial norms give the inverse-moment coefficients of K_epsilon-K_0. Substitution u=1/(1+v) gives exactly an e^{i eta} Tricomi U(n+1,-alpha,-i eta) ratio, and the large-first-parameter U/Bessel expansion yields d_n=-epsilon sqrt(pi) eta^((2 alpha+1)/4)/(Gamma(alpha+1)Gamma(alpha+2)) n^((6 alpha+5)/4) exp(-sqrt(2 eta n)) times [cos(sqrt(2 eta n)+eta/2-pi(2 alpha+1)/8)+O(n^-1/2)]. The reciprocal correction is exponentially smaller. Fourier coefficients imply globally G^2 boundary trace, and a near-maximal-phase integer subsequence precludes any G^sigma, sigma<2. The original singular term is excluded; no pointwise non-Gevrey or parameter-uniform claim is made.
